sources.name: Tech Insider: ChatGPT Go vs Plus vs Pro

caption:
Grok costs $30 a month for SuperGrok. ChatGPT Plus costs $20.
Grok can search live X posts. ChatGPT has the bigger toolbox: Codex, agent mode, apps and integrations.
Here is where each one wins.

Which one do you actually use every day?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: xAI, X and OpenAI help centers, Lindy, Zapier · Photo: Tekedia
threads_text: Grok vs ChatGPT comes down to one thing: Grok reads live X posts, ChatGPT has the bigger toolbox. SuperGrok is $30 a month, ChatGPT Plus is $20. Which one would you pay for?

site_article.headline: Grok vs ChatGPT: where each one wins, plans and prices compared
site_article.dek: Grok searches live X posts and makes images and video; ChatGPT has the wider set of tools. SuperGrok costs $30 a month, ChatGPT Plus $20.
site_article.summary: Grok and ChatGPT handle everyday chat about equally well, but they are built around different strengths. Grok is tied to X and live search, while ChatGPT offers more tools, apps and integrations for $10 less a month at the main paid tier.
site_article.seo_title: Grok vs ChatGPT: where each one wins, plans compared
site_article.seo_description: Grok vs ChatGPT compared: live X search, tools, images and video, usage limits, privacy and plan prices, plus which one to pick for your work.
site_article.answer_summary: Pick Grok if you want live X posts and image or video generation in one app. Pick ChatGPT for most other work: it has more tools and integrations, and Plus costs $20 against $30 for SuperGrok.
site_article.hero_alt: A phone showing Elon Musk's face held in front of a screen with the word Grok and the xAI logo.

paragraphs.text: Grok vs ChatGPT is one of the most searched AI comparisons. Grok, from xAI, works at grok.com, in its iOS and Android apps and inside X. ChatGPT, from OpenAI, is the assistant most people try first. Both have free plans, and their main paid tiers cost $30 and $20 a month.

This guide compares the two for everyday use, based on xAI's and X's help pages, OpenAI's help center, two plan breakdowns updated in October and November 2026 and Zapier's side by side review. It does not crown a smarter model, because both companies ship new models every few months. Prices can differ by country and app store, so check at checkout.
Grok vs ChatGPT: the short answer

For most people, ChatGPT is the safer first pick: it costs less at the main paid tier and does more things inside one app. Grok earns its place if you live on X, want to know what people are posting in the last few hours, or want image and video generation in the same subscription. Plenty of people keep a free account on one and pay for the other.

Zapier's review, last updated in April 2026, reached a similar verdict. It found the two about even on everyday tasks and called ChatGPT the more mature product and the better value at $20, while noting that Grok's top plan can run several agents at once and combine their results.
Where Grok wins: live X posts
X's help center says Grok can decide by itself whether to search public X posts or run a real-time web search to answer a question. Inside X, you open it from the Grok icon in the navigation bar.

That access cuts both ways. X's own help page calls Grok an early version that may confidently give incorrect information, missummarize or miss context, and asks users to verify anything important. Zapier's reviewer also saw offensive posts surface when asking about controversial topics.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: A live check you can verify
paragraphs.text:
Search X and the web for what people are saying about [topic] in the last 24 hours.
Separate confirmed facts from rumors.
Link every post and article you used.
Open the links before you repeat anything. If Grok gives a claim with no link, treat it as unverified.
Where ChatGPT wins: tools and integrations

Zapier lists Codex for coding, Canvas, agent mode, custom GPTs, scheduled tasks and dedicated Windows and Mac apps among ChatGPT's tools, plus native integrations with Google Drive, GitHub, Slack, Photoshop and Canva. Its review put Codex well ahead of Grok for coding.

ChatGPT also searches the web. OpenAI's help center says you can pick Web search from the plus menu or by typing a slash, and answers can show inline citations with a Sources section that lists the cited links.
xAI has added more tools of its own. Its FAQ describes Grok Build, which replaced Grok Studio, and Grok Bot, a separate product with AI teammates on a cloud computer, connectors and routines.
Files, images and video

Grok accepts large uploads. xAI's FAQ says you can attach about 100 files to one message on the web and 20 on Android, most up to 150 MB, including PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, images, audio and MP4 or MOV video.

Grok generates images and video. Every result carries a Grok watermark, there is no setting to remove it, and xAI's rules forbid hiding it. Zapier reported that Grok's image generation was turned off for free users after a deepfake scandal and is included from SuperGrok Lite.

ChatGPT makes images on every plan, with limited creation on Free, higher limits on Go and more complex and accurate images on Plus, according to Tech Insider's November 2026 plan breakdown. Zapier said ChatGPT excels at images and puts safety first.
Limits: how each one counts your usage

Since June 2026, paid Grok plans share one weekly usage pool across chat, image and video, voice, Build and API use, and each product costs a different amount. You can see what you have used under Settings, then Usage. When the pool runs out, paid features pause unless you buy Extra Usage Credits, which start at $5 on the web, or upgrade. Free limits for chat and voice stay separate.

ChatGPT limits depend on the plan. Tech Insider says Plus gets 5 scheduled tasks and up to 3 hours a day of GPT-Live voice, while Pro gets 15 tasks and up to 15 hours on the $100 plan. Dot, OpenAI's always-on agent, is only on Pro.
Price: the plans side by side

Lindy's October 2026 breakdown lists Grok Free, SuperGrok Lite at $10 a month, SuperGrok at $30 or $300 a year, SuperGrok Plus at $100 with 1080p video, and SuperGrok Heavy at $300. X Premium at $8 a month raises Grok limits, and Premium+ at $40 includes SuperGrok access.

For ChatGPT, Tech Insider lists Free, Go, Plus at $20 a month and Pro plans at $100, $200 and $500. Plus runs on GPT-6 Sol by default, while Free and Go use GPT-6 Luna. Some Go users in select regions see ads in a test.
Privacy settings worth changing

X says it may share your public data and your Grok conversations with xAI to train models. To opt out, open Settings, then Privacy and safety, then Data sharing and personalization, then Grok and Third-party Collaborators, and clear Data Sharing. Thumbs up or down feedback may still be used.
On either assistant, do not paste passwords, health records or other private details. X's help page asks for exactly that with Grok.
Which one to pick

paragraphs.title: 1. You follow news and X all day
paragraphs.text: Pick Grok. Live X search is the one thing it does that ChatGPT does not, and SuperGrok adds images and video in the same plan.

paragraphs.title: 2. You write, code or automate
paragraphs.text: Pick ChatGPT. Plus costs $20, and Codex, agent mode and its integrations cover more of a working day.

paragraphs.title: 3. You are not sure
paragraphs.text: Use both free plans for a week and run the same prompts in each, then pay for the one you kept opening.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: A fair side by side test
paragraphs.text:
I need to [task, for example plan a three day trip to Chicago on a $600 budget].
Ask me up to three questions first.
Then give me the plan as a short checklist, and list any facts I should double check with a link for each.

What each is bad at: Grok can repeat what is trending on X before it is confirmed, and its weekly pool is shared by chat, images, video and voice, so heavy use of one leaves less for the rest. ChatGPT may answer from memory when it does not search, so turn on search for anything recent, and its strongest models sit behind the paid plans.
